title: Preflight validation and fair-share queue orchestration for Dedicated reservations
creator: Ethan Morris
description: Problem: Customers request Dedicated capacity that sometimes fails provisioning due to mismatched packing profiles, incompatible autoscale policies, or unrealistic throughput targets. That results in manual back-and-forth, delayed onboarding, and overprovisioning. This ticket scopes a preflight validation + fair-share queuing mechanism that: 1) validates reservation requests against fleet constraints and model-characteristic heuristics at intake, 2) assigns requests to a priority/fair-share queue with simulated canary estimates, and 3) exposes actionable guidance to customers (expected wait, minimum commit, suggested policy adjustments). Goal is to reduce manual provisioning cycles by 50%, improve on-time provisioning SLO from 68% to 90%, and reduce wasted capacity during onboarding by 30%.
acceptance_criteria: Intake API rejects reservation requests that violate hard constraints (region unavailable, incompatible hardware type, model > max sequence length for chosen GPU class) with actionable error codes and suggested fixes.

Queue allocator assigns queued requests a numeric fair-share score based on (customer tier, request age, requested throughput, historical utilization) and exposes position and ETA in Console and intake API.

Preflight simulator returns a canary throughput and latency estimate for the requested configuration (including autoscaling min/max), and shows alternate lower-cost options (quantized model, smaller instance type, relaxed throughput) with estimated cost delta.
Onboarding runbook documents steps for ops to manually approve high-risk requests; automated approvals execute if preflight passes and score >= threshold.
Metrics: provisioning turn-around median drops to <= 3 business days for standard requests and <= 1 business day for expedited tier (verified in dashboard).
End-to-end E2E tests validating intake -> queue -> provision flow exist in CI and are green.
design_decisions: Perform lightweight syntactic + semantic checks at intake (no live fleet queries) to provide immediate feedback; follow with asynchronous fleet topology check that can defer provisioning into queue.
Fair-share score formula: 40% customer tier, 30% request age, 20% requested throughput normalized to fleet supply, 10% historical on-time payments/commitment reliability.

Simulator will use historical kernel scheduling profiles and recent sequence-length distributions for the requested model family; we will not run a full model trace in preflight to keep compute costs low.
Expose suggested mitigations in the Console as ordered options (e.g., enable 4-bit quantization, reduce target RPS by 30%, switch to a compatible model variant).
Automated approval only for requests that: pass topology checks, fair-share score >= 0.75, and preflight simulator predicts latency and cost within policy SLAs.
implementation_notes: Backend: Extend intake-service with synchronous validation layer + async queueing job. Add QueueAllocator service with pluggable scoring function.
Console: New queue-status card on Dedicated onboarding flow showing position, ETA, suggested changes, and 'request expedited review' button.
Data: New BigQuery table 'reservation_preflight_runs' capturing input, result, score, and timestamp for observability and ML tuning of the scoring weights.
E2E: Add a test harness that replays representative intake payloads and asserts expected queue assignment and provisioning outcome.
Security: Preflight outputs may include inferred customer usage patterns; restrict access to Ops + request owner and log to audit trail.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Scoring formula unfairly deprioritizes legitimate low-tier customers. Mitigation: run offline fairness analysis on 6 months of historical requests and add a fairness floor so no customer is starved for > 14 days.
Risk: Simulator estimates under/over fit real throughput. Mitigation: run AB test on 5% of requests with both simulated and observed outcomes; update kernel profile weights monthly.
Risk: Adding preflight latency increases perceived signup friction. Mitigation: keep synchronous checks microsecond-scale; show progress and allow users to continue while async checks complete.
Risk: Ops churn from new UI elements. Mitigation: include an in-Console help tour and a one-week ops-shadowing period where product team fields questions.

notes: We will run a 4-week pilot with three anchor customers (one AI-native startup, one mid-market SaaS, one enterprise with high SLOs). Pilot acceptance criteria: average provisioning TAT <= 3 days and <10% manual interventions. After pilot, iterate scoring weights and promote to GA with a migration playbook for existing queued requests.
